reviews.verdict: A genuinely sophisticated ratings engine and top-decile listing craft idling at 2 total ratings — the bottleneck is native install volume and a stale, half-shipped Play presence, not the quality of the ask.
strengths: Native ask placement is excellent: fires only at emotional peaks (Footle solve gated on >=1 prior-day solve, perfect or >=90% quiz scores, 7/30/100 streak milestones, live MP win with >=2 players and no draw), never stacks on the notification sheet, 45-day cooldown, and the lifetime cap was correctly raised 4->24 after diagnosing that iOS's silent no-ops were burning the allowance on the most engaged users (src/lib/review.js:14-27, src/App.jsx:9403-9416, 9613-9620, src/screens/OnlineMultiplayer.jsx:836-848).

A real bad-experience deflector exists on the custom web prompt: 'Not really' routes to a mailto feedback draft, 'never the store' (src/App.jsx:8150, 10833-10837) — and the native path deliberately has no pre-gate, which is the policy-compliant choice (Google's in-app review policy forbids gating the native card; happy-moment-only triggering is the legal equivalent of a deflector).

Too-early asks are prevented on every path: Footle requires a solve on an earlier day ('rating an app on the first puzzle you ever played is how you collect three-star ratings', App.jsx:9405-9413), the quiz path requires >=5 lifetime games (newTotal >= 5, App.jsx:9617), the web card requires 5+ games and a 9+/10 score and fires once ever (App.jsx:9656-9664).

Listing craft is exceptional for a solo dev: a factually wrong Footle paragraph and a false 'every answer has an explanation' claim were caught and fixed against measured numbers (81.8%), keywords were de-duplicated across fields, the US locale gets 'Soccer Quiz' while GB gets 'Football Quiz', first-3 screenshots curated for the install sheet (store-assets/1.6.1/LISTING.md sections 2b, 4, 6).

15 full store localisations exist with per-locale names, subtitles, keywords and whatsNew (store-assets/1.6.1/localisations.json: en-GB/US/CA/AU, es-ES/MX, pt-BR/PT, tr, fr, fr-CA, de, it, id, ar), and all 15 privacy-policy URLs were set and verified.

The iOS average that exists is perfect — 5.0 stars (apps.apple.com/gb/app/id6775975961) — so there is nothing to repair, only volume to build; and the 1.6.1 Play release notes are reader-quality, tagged <en-US>, 439 chars under the 500 cap (store-assets/1.6.1/play-release-notes.txt).
weaknesses: Output is near-zero: 2 ratings on the GB App Store storefront (5.0 avg), 'hasn't received enough ratings' on the US storefront, no displayable rating at all on Google Play (no aggregateRating in the live page's JSON-LD), and a '50+' downloads band — at this volume a single 1-star drops the visible average to 3.0, so 4.8+ is a volume problem before it is anything else.

The live Play listing is STALE: title still 'Ball IQ: Football Trivia' and the old short description ('Soccer & football trivia quizzes, Footle & live multiplayer...') are what shoppers see today — the rewritten copy sits in a staged draft behind the vc19 review; the required 1024x500 feature graphic does not exist anywhere in the repo (find returned nothing; PLAY-LISTING.md lists it as open); the 15 localised Play listings are unapplied despite the copy existing.

Daily 7 — the #2 mode at 48 players/30d — can never trigger the native ask: mode !== 'daily' at src/App.jsx:9617 blocks it, and 7/30/100 streak milestones are swallowed whenever they land on a daily results screen; the engine's best moments in the second-most-played mode are structurally unreachable.

15-language store listings promise an experience the English-only app cannot deliver — the ES/PT/BR download-then-disappoint pattern is the single biggest structural threat to holding 4.8+ once rating volume arrives (localised listing copy in localisations.json vs. app UI English-only per shared facts).

No sentiment suppression on the native path: a user who just reported a broken question or hit an error can still get the review sheet 3.5s into their next win — the deflector is moment-based, not user-based.

The 1.6.1 whatsNew is written for all 15 locales but flagged NOT YET APPLIED in either console (localisations.json _status: '1.6.1 RELEASE NOTES WRITTEN 2026-08-18 — NOT YET APPLIED'), and the OnlineMultiplayer comment claims 'fires once' / first-win semantics while the code fires on every MP-win screen mount (harmless via cooldown, but the comment lies).

reviews.verdict: Fairness and honesty are A-grade and freshly battle-tested by actual play, but the sensory payoff is uneven — Mystery wins in total silence, the entire sound layer ships dark by default, and the one player who never saw the answer (timeout) gets the shortest look at it.
strengths: Honesty culture is elite: timeouts now say 'Time's up' instead of lying (App.jsx:2174-2181), timed-out questions join the review WITH explanations (App.jsx:2453-2469), Mystery's give-up panel deliberately refuses win styling (MysteryPlayer.jsx:275-278), and fake percentile social proof was removed for honest tier copy (App.jsx:4295-4312).

Losing feels fair, Duolingo-grade: daily streaks tick on ANY completion win-or-loss, streak shields exist, and a dead streak gets an empathetic rebuild toast ('day X of the rebuild. Your best: N' — App.jsx:8355-8368) instead of silent reset.

Rich haptic vocabulary — six distinct native patterns (correct/wrong/hardCorrect/heavy/select/levelup) mapped to specific moments, with web vibrate fallbacks (App.jsx:1910-1941), plus a dedicated hard-question particle burst and 'HARD - NAILED IT' badge (App.jsx:2500-2522).

Real celebration infrastructure: confetti at >=80% (App.jsx:4557), CountUp score with haptic-on-land (App.jsx:4637), XP promoted into the hero moment in gold (App.jsx:4664-4672), milestone confetti at 7/30/100-day streaks (App.jsx:8377-8387).

The worst pace bugs were caught by playing THIS WEEK and fixed: double-tap re-entry guard (633 dead clicks, skipped questions — App.jsx:2216-2227), answered option cards now advance on tap instead of being dead (App.jsx:2676-2687), and a finished day routes onward to yesterday's puzzles or Survival (DailyScreen.jsx:258-294).

Footle nails the Wordle drama beat-for-beat: 280ms staggered tile flips (TIMINGS.WORDLE_FLIP_MS, App.jsx:7434), graded keyboard state, haptic+sound at the moment of truth, confetti gated to fresh solves only (App.jsx:7631).
weaknesses: Mystery Player's win is completely mute: grep for haptic/playSound/Confetti in MysteryPlayer.jsx returns ZERO matches — no buzz on the winning guess, no confetti, no sound, just a green panel. The hardest, longest-effort daily has the flattest payoff, while Trail gets Confetti+hardCorrect haptic (TransferTrail.jsx:117,198) and Footle gets all three. Wrong Mystery guesses also give nothing — no shake, no haptic — where Trail shakes and buzzes.

The entire audio design is unheard by most players: sound defaults to FALSE (App.jsx:8114 'sound:false, haptics:true'), so the carefully-built chimes, streak arpeggio, and daily_complete chord (App.jsx:1795-1833) play to almost nobody. Duolingo ships sound on.

Timeouts auto-advance after 800ms (App.jsx:2331) while wrong answers wait for a Next tap — the one case where the player has NO idea what the answer was gets the shortest dwell. The review-screen fix (App.jsx:2453-2469) patches this after the fact, but the in-moment reveal is still rushed.

No in-run streak feedback on mobile outside Survival: the streak pill is desktop-only and aria-hidden (App.jsx:2609-2610, base display:none), so a 5-in-a-row mid-quiz passes in silence — the combo dopamine Wordle/Duolingo mine relentlessly is left on the table until the results screen.

Mystery's core steering signal is known-corrupted: similarity() scores nationality, and the file's own header documents that `nat` is wrong for marquee players (Messi/Vinicius/James all read 'Spain'), so 'wherever nat is wrong the RANKS are wrong too' (MysteryPlayer.jsx:13-41). A player steering by rank can be honestly misled by the mechanic itself.

The daily_complete celebration chord + heavy haptic only fires for Daily 7 (App.jsx:9801-9803, inside handleComplete); Footle/Trail/Mystery completions dispatch biq:daily-completed but never get that shell-level payoff.

quick_wins.what: Port Trail's feedback into Mystery: haptic('hardCorrect') + Confetti on the winning guess, haptic('wrong') on a cold one — the imports are one line (Trail already imports both from ../App.jsx at TransferTrail.jsx:24) and Trail is the exact template.

Route timeouts through the same showNext dwell as wrong answers (or extend 800ms to ~2.5s) so the revealed answer and explanation are actually readable in the moment — change is one branch in advance() at App.jsx:2331.
Fire haptic('heavy') + the daily_complete chord from the biq:daily-completed handler for Footle/Trail/Mystery, not just Daily 7 — the event already carries game + won.

reviews.verdict: The on-device habit loop is genuinely well-built and live (streak, auto-shields, win-back local notifications, day-complete routing), but the reminder channel reaches almost nobody — 0 web-push subscribers on the surface carrying 60% of sessions, 9 remote notifications ever sent, ~34 opted-in native devices — so the loop only retains people already inside it, which is exactly what flat DAU 13-17 through 111 signups/30d looks like.
strengths: Streak design is more forgiving than NYT's and it's deliberate: streak ticks on ANY daily completion, win or loss (src/App.jsx:9382-9394, citing NYT's 5.6M lost streaks), shields auto-consume on a single missed day with no manual step (src/App.jsx:8297-8299, 10421-10424), earned 1 per 200 XP capped at 3 banked (src/App.jsx:8288), server-authoritative via tick_login_streak RPC for signed-in users (src/App.jsx:8262) plus a one-off grace shield migration (v1_5_streak_grace_shield.sql).

The native reminder engine is complete and shipped since ~1.1 (commit 7e3d139, win-back tail d46f4b0 2026-07-03): 7pm-local nudge only if unplayed, cancelled the moment they play (src/lib/notifications.js:76-120), rotating copy, plus a decaying win-back tail at days 8/11/15/22/30 so lapsed users stay reachable (src/lib/notifications.js:24-30) — the file's own comment calls going silent after 7 days 'the single biggest retention hole' and fixes it.

Opt-in etiquette is thoughtful: soft in-app pre-prompt capped at 2 lifetime asks, fired after the first daily and again at a 3-day streak, delayed 7s so it never covers the answer reveal or the Share button (src/App.jsx:9282-9320, 9521-9528).

Tomorrow has a reason: four frozen daily modes, a 14-day W/D form strip in football idiom (src/screens/DailyScreen.jsx:534, 745-746), streak milestones celebrated at 7/30/100 (src/App.jsx:9591-9597), a 'New puzzles in Xh' countdown (DailyScreen.jsx:863), and a DayComplete panel that routes a finished day into yesterday's unplayed puzzles or Survival instead of a dead wall (DailyScreen.jsx:258-294).

The streak loop demonstrably works for the core: prod shows 32 signed-in users active today/yesterday and 17 holding a live streak >=2 (user_game_state.login_streak query, 2026-08-19) — roughly the whole DAU is streak-carrying.

A yesterday-only catch-up already exists (replay glyph + DayComplete offers), and the code documents that a 30-day back-catalogue is 'one gate away' behind a known accounting fix (DailyScreen.jsx:233-237).
weaknesses: The brief's premise 'no push notifications' is wrong — three layers exist (LocalNotifications, web push, APNs) — but the measured reach makes it functionally true: public.notifications contains 9 rows ALL TIME (5 play_invite, 1 friend_request, 1 friend_accept, 1 generic, 1 daily_reminder test on 2026-08-14), so the remote pipeline has effectively never fired for a real user.

Web push is fully deployed (sw.js v10 push handlers, src/lib/webpush.js, send-web-push edge fn, hourly pg_cron 'web-daily-reminder' live in prod) yet has ZERO subscribers — because the only opt-in surface is a Settings toggle (src/App.jsx:6220) and the soft pre-prompt no-ops on web (notificationsSupported() is native-only, src/App.jsx:9292). 60% of sessions are web/organic: the biggest audience has no reminder channel at all.

The reachable audience is ~34 devices (device_tokens count in prod) against 173 users with streak state and 111 signups/30d — the reminder engine, however good, addresses under a third of even the signed-in base.

Android has no remote push at all: no google-services.json, and src/lib/push.js:20 says 'iOS ONLY for now' — Android users get local reminders only, and Android 1.5.1 users in prod today predate several retention fixes.

No email channel exists anywhere (no SMTP/resend/sendgrid sender in src/ or supabase/functions; balliq.app email is inbound-only), and no home-screen/lock-screen widget (ios/App contains only the App target) — the two channels that don't require a permission prompt are both absent.

APNs push was 'SILENTLY DEAD' until the v1_5 fix (supabase/migrations/v1_5_fix_service_role_push_reads.sql:1) — symptomatic of the repo-wide pattern: retention loops get built end-to-end but nobody measures whether they deliver, so they leak at the last step.

quick_wins.what: Surface web-push opt-in at the post-solve happy moment: extend the existing maybePromptNotif soft-prompt pattern (src/App.jsx:9291) to browsers where webPushSupported() is true, calling the already-built enableWebPush(). Every downstream piece — SW handlers, edge fn, hourly cron — is deployed and was end-to-end tested 2026-08-14; this converts 0 subscribers on the 60%-of-sessions surface into a real channel with one UI change.

Make the web daily-reminder body streak-aware at send time (the cron runs live, so unlike pre-scheduled local notifications it CAN know the streak): join user_game_state.login_streak in enqueue_web_daily_reminders (v1_5_web_daily_reminder_cron.sql:22-24) so the nudge says 'your 12-day streak ends tonight' — the copy Duolingo has A/B-proven for a decade.

Fix the live-vs-archive accounting gate (documented at src/screens/DailyScreen.jsx:233-237) so form14 and the guest streak walk distinguish archive plays, then open the 30-day back-catalogue the code says is 'one gate away' — a lapsed player who returns should find a week of content, not one stale day.

Instrument the funnel you can't currently see: log biq_notif_enabled / notif_asks outcomes and web-push permission results to a tiny analytics table, so 'how many of 173 users can we reach' becomes a number instead of the 34-token proxy.

five_star_moves: Reach parity with the traffic: web-push opt-in prompted in-flow (not buried in Settings), FCM for Android remote push, and an email capture + weekly digest fallback for the permission-decliners — Duolingo's retention is the channel stack (push + email + widget), not the streak math, and Ball IQ has only built the streak math's equal.

An iOS home/lock-screen widget showing today's four modes done/undone + streak flame — Wordle and NYT Games' widget is the zero-permission daily trigger that survives notification fatigue; Ball IQ's daily-status data model (matchdays/form14) already computes everything the widget would render.

Streak repair as a comeback moment (Duolingo-style): when a streak dies un-shielded, offer one restore via playing yesterday's open puzzles within 48h — the DayComplete/yesterdayOpen plumbing (DailyScreen.jsx:238-256) is 80% of this feature.

Social pull: surface friends' streaks and a weekly friends' form-strip comparison — the notification inbox, friendships table, and APNs trigger already exist, but today nothing in the social graph generates a reason to return (5 play invites in the app's lifetime).

reviews.verdict: Five unusually well-crafted share loops with real OG cards and 1-tap play for recipients, but no evidence any of them closes at volume — referral traffic was 11 sessions/week, native-app shares are invisible to the instrumentation, and the highest-intent loop (MP invite) still walls the friend behind account creation.
strengths: Tap economy is excellent: every great moment has share one tap from the results surface (App.jsx:4713-4714 'Share Score' + 'Stump a mate' in the action stack; Footle end screen App.jsx:7654 plus a dedicated one-tap 'Share on WhatsApp' on web at 7666), so sender friction is 2-3 taps total to a friend's chat.

Recipient-side design is the real standout: 4 of 5 loops are zero-login, 1-tap-to-playing. Stump links open a single guest-playable question with a 'Pass it on' chain CTA (App.jsx:4478, api/q.js:47); /c/ challenge recipients play the same deterministic Daily 7 and get a head-to-head modal with 'Send it back 🔁' (App.jsx:10948); balliq.app/footle boots straight into the game (vercel.json:104-105).

Every link unfurls as a server-rendered card, not a bare URL: api/q.js redacts the answer so the mystery is the hook, api/c.js renders a taunt card with name + score dots, api/iq.js renders a club-coloured score card — all edge functions with per-hit bot/human logging.

The /iq/ club-score loop routes humans to the CLUB PAGE, not /play (api/iq.js:6-12, explicitly reasoned: 94.6% of sessions view one page, so the club page is where the loop can regenerate) — the one loop aligned with where the actual traffic is (club pages = 7 of top-10 landing pages).

Share copy shows real virality thinking: self-deprecating framing beats bragging ('It got me too 🙈 can YOU get it?' App.jsx:4441, chosen deliberately per comment at 4572), deep links land recipients in the exact quiz they were beaten at (App.jsx:9843-9845), and Snapchat/iMessage payload quirks are individually handled (App.jsx:4014-4029).

Both ends are instrumented: loopEvent Clarity events at every share invocation and token consumption (App.jsx:3995, 7990, 8570, 10494) plus edge-side loop-hit logs distinguishing OG-crawler unfurls from human click-throughs (api/c.js:22-28) — the k-factor question is answerable in principle.
weaknesses: The MP invite loop — the only one where a friend is literally waiting for you — gates the recipient behind sign-in: 'We'll drop you straight into the room as soon as you're signed in' (App.jsx:11269-11284). Account creation before fun is exactly the last-step leak the opportunity scan named, on the loop with the strongest social pull.

The sender never learns their challenge was played. /c/ tokens are stateless (score.date.name in the URL, nothing stored server-side, api/c.js:32-47), so there is no 'Marius played your challenge' moment — the loop closes emotionally only for the recipient. Combined with no reward of any kind for sharing, senders have no reason to share twice.

K-factor is structurally unmeasurable for the users who matter: loopEvent is web-only by construction — 'Clarity never loads in the native shell' (App.jsx:1849-1850) — so every share from the iOS/Android apps is invisible on the send side. Instrumentation also only landed 2026-08-10, nine days ago.

No loop is proven to close: the one referral number observed in the codebase is '11 referral sessions in the week to 2026-08-13' (gen-seo-pages.mjs:1241-1242) against 60% organic search.
